---

The official Java library for the Tungo Platform API (`https://api.tungo.kz`): the AI accountant, 1C integration, bank statements, e-invoices, tax forms and automations of [Tungo AI](https://tungo.kz).

It is generated from the API's OpenAPI contract, so its methods and models always match the contract it was built from.

## Requirements

Java 11 or later. The library uses the JDK's `java.net.http.HttpClient` and depends only on [Jackson](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson) (`jackson-databind` with `jackson-core` and `jackson-annotations`), version 2.14 or later; the build declares 2.22.4. CI runs on Java 11, 17, 21 and 25.

## Installation

Maven:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>kz.tungo</groupId>
  <artifactId>tungo-sdk</artifactId>
  <version>0.3.0</version> <!-- x-release-version -->
</dependency>
```

Gradle:

```kotlin
implementation("kz.tungo:tungo-sdk:0.3.0") // x-release-version
```

The automatic module name is `kz.tungo.sdk`. The code of this README lives in [`examples/`](examples) and is compiled and run by the test suite.

## Quick start

```java
TungoClient client = TungoClient.builder()
    .apiKey("tg_...") // or leave it out and set TUNGO_API_KEY
    .build();

for (CompanyListItem company : client.companies().list().data()) {
    System.out.println(company.id() + " " + company.name());
}

ChatTurnResult turn = client.ask("co_...", "Сколько НДС к уплате за этот квартал?");
System.out.println(turn.answer());
```

## Authentication and configuration

Create one client and share it: it is immutable and safe to use from several threads or tasks. Every option can be passed explicitly; three of them fall back to environment variables.

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `TUNGO_API_KEY` | none |
| Base URL | `TUNGO_BASE_URL` | `https://api.tungo.kz` |
| Webhook secret | `TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | none |
| Timeout | | 60 s (600 s for non-streaming chat turns) |
| Maximum retries | | 2 |
| Default headers, HTTP client | | none, built-in |

The API key is sent only to operations that require it; public endpoints and incoming hooks never receive it, and it never appears in error messages or debug output. Calling an authenticated operation without a key fails locally, before any request is made.

Every method also accepts per-request options: timeout, maximum retries, extra headers, an idempotency key and cancellation.

```java
TungoClient client = TungoClient.builder()
    .apiKey(System.getenv("TUNGO_API_KEY"))
    .baseUrl("https://api.tungo.kz")
    .webhookSecret(System.getenv("TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET"))
    .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))
    .maxRetries(3)
    .defaultHeader("X-App", "ledger-sync")
    .httpClient(myHttpClient) // optional: your own java.net.http.HttpClient (proxy, TLS, ...)
    .build();

// Per-request options are accepted by every method.
Company company = client.companies().get("co_...", RequestOptions.builder()
    .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
    .maxRetries(0)
    .header("X-Trace-Id", "trace-123")
    .build());
```

`TungoClient.fromEnv()` builds a client from the environment variables alone. `RequestOptions` is accepted by every method. A thread interrupt aborts a request, a retry delay, a stream read or a wait with `InterruptedRequestException`, and the interrupt flag stays set. `client.close()` releases the threads the client created; an `HttpClient` or executor you supplied is left alone.

## Errors

Every failure is a subtype of the SDK's base error. An HTTP error response becomes an API error chosen by the `error.type` field of the response body, falling back to the HTTP status when the body is not the API's error envelope:

| `error.type` | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request_error` | 400 |
| `authentication_error` | 401 |
| `payment_required_error` | 402 |
| `permission_error` | 403 |
| `not_found_error` | 404 |
| `conflict_error` | 409 |
| `gone_error` | 410 |
| `limit_error` | 429 |
| `api_error` | 500 |
| `unavailable_error` | 503 |

An API error carries the status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, the parsed retry-after delay, the response headers and the raw body. Problems that happen without a response have their own types: connection error, timeout, decode error (a successful response whose body is not valid), and configuration or validation error (raised before any request).

```java
try {
    client.companies().get("co_missing");
    outcome = "found";
} catch (NotFoundException e) {
    outcome = "not found, request " + e.requestId().orElse("?");
} catch (LimitException e) {
    outcome = "limited, retry after " + e.retryAfter().map(Duration::toString).orElse("?");
} catch (ApiException e) {
    // status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, headers, raw body
    outcome = e.statusCode() + " " + e.type() + " " + e.code().orElse("") + " " + e.fields();
} catch (TungoException e) {
    // connection errors, timeouts, undecodable responses, local validation
    outcome = e.getMessage();
}
```

All exceptions are unchecked and extend `TungoException`: `ApiException` (an HTTP error; the subclass is chosen by `error.type`: `InvalidRequestException`, `AuthenticationException`, `PaymentRequiredException`, `PermissionDeniedException`, `NotFoundException`, `ConflictException`, `GoneException`, `LimitException`, `InternalServerException`, `UnavailableException`), `ConnectionException`, `TungoTimeoutException` (and `WaitTimeoutException` for the waiting helpers), `DecodeException`, `ConfigException`, `ValidationException`, `PaginationException`, `InterruptedRequestException` and `WebhookVerificationException`. When a failure wraps another exception (an I/O error, a parser error), that exception is in `getCause()`.

## Retries and timeouts

A request is retried up to 2 times (3 attempts) on connection errors, timeouts and the statuses 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, but only when repeating it is safe: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT` and `DELETE` requests, and `POST` or `PATCH` requests of the operations whose contract declares an `Idempotency-Key`. For those the SDK generates a random key and reuses it for every attempt; you can pass your own. Other operations send no key, not even one you pass, because the API would ignore it.

The delay between attempts is `min(0.5 s × 2^attempt, 8 s)` with random jitter. A positive `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After` response header overrides it; if the server asks for more than 60 s the SDK does not wait and raises the error with the delay filled in.

The timeout covers the whole request including reading the body. Streaming calls have no total timeout, only a connect timeout and an idle timeout of 120 s. Cancellation supplied by the caller is combined with the timeout.

```java
// Defaults: 2 retries (3 attempts), 60 s per request, 600 s for a non-streaming chat turn.
TungoClient client = TungoClient.builder()
    .maxRetries(5)
    .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(20))
    .build();

ChatTurnResult turn = client.ask("co_...", "Проверь выписку", RequestOptions.builder()
    .timeout(Duration.ofMinutes(2))
    .maxRetries(1)
    .idempotencyKey("ask-2026-11-09-001") // generated automatically when left out
    .build());
```

A `POST` or `PATCH` is retried only when it carries an `Idempotency-Key`; the SDK generates one for the operations whose contract declares the header and reuses it across attempts.

## Pagination

List operations use cursor pagination (`{ data, next_cursor }`). The plain method returns one typed page that knows whether there is a next page and can fetch it. The auto-paging variant is a lazy iterator: it requests the next page only when needed, carries your filters over, and stops fetching as soon as you stop iterating.

```java
ProposalsListParams filter = ProposalsListParams.builder().status("pending").limit(50).build();

// One page at a time.
Page<ProposalListItem, ProposalPage> page = client.proposals().list("co_...", filter);
for (ProposalListItem proposal : page.data()) {
    ids.add(proposal.id());
}
if (page.hasNextPage()) {
    page = page.nextPage(); // same filter, next cursor
}

// Or every item of every page, fetched lazily.
for (ProposalListItem proposal : client.proposals().listAll("co_...", filter)) {
    System.out.println(proposal.id() + " " + proposal.kindTitle());
}
long total = client.proposals().listAll("co_...", filter).stream().count();
```

`Page.body()` gives the whole typed page for list operations that return more than `data` and `next_cursor`. `listAll(...)` is lazy: it fetches the next page only when the iteration reaches it. A list response without its `data` array is a `DecodeException`, not an empty page; a cursor the server already returned on the way (the same one again, or a cycle) ends the iteration with `PaginationException`.

## Streaming

Streaming operations use server-sent events and deliver typed events as they arrive. Leaving the loop early or closing the stream closes the connection. A stream request is retried only before its first byte; an error response is raised as the same typed API error as for ordinary calls. A chat stream that ends before its final event is reported as an error, never as a finished answer.

```java
ChatMessageRequest question = ChatMessageRequest.builder().message("Что с НДС за квартал?").build();
try (ChatStream stream = client.chat().createStream("co_...", question)) {
    for (ChatEvent event : stream) {
        if (event instanceof ChatEventText) {
            text.append(((ChatEventText) event).delta());
        } else if (event instanceof ChatEventTool) {
            System.out.println("tool: " + ((ChatEventTool) event).name());
        } else if (event instanceof ChatEventDone) {
            System.out.println("stop reason: " + ((ChatEventDone) event).stopReason().orElse("?"));
        }
    }
    System.out.println("dialog " + stream.dialogId().orElse("?"));
}

// Or let the SDK collect the answer. A mid-stream error event is thrown as an ApiException,
// a stream that ends before its "done" event as a DecodeException.
ChatStreamResult result = client.askStream("co_...", "Что с НДС за квартал?").accumulate();
System.out.println(result.text() + " (" + result.stopReason().orElse("?") + ")");
```

A stream holds a connection: always close it (try-with-resources). The same types serve `chat().answerStream`, `chat().listEvents`, `batches().listEvents` and `feed().listEvents` (an `EventStream<FeedItem>`). A stream has no total timeout, only the idle timeout (120 s by default). Iterating simply ends when the server closes the stream, but `accumulate()` returns only a finished turn: if the stream ends before its `done` event (a cut connection, an early `close()`), it throws `DecodeException` instead of returning the partial text. A success response that is not `text/event-stream` is a `DecodeException` as well. The exception is a finished chat turn that the API replays for a repeated `Idempotency-Key` (`application/json` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`): its stored result arrives as the events of that turn, ending with `done`.

## Webhooks

Outgoing webhooks are signed according to the Standard Webhooks specification (Svix). The verify helper takes the raw request body and the headers (`webhook-*` or `svix-*`), checks the HMAC-SHA256 signature in constant time and the timestamp within 300 s of the system clock, and returns the typed event. Any problem is reported as a webhook verification error. If no secret is passed, the client's webhook secret is used.

The send-hook helper posts an event to an incoming hook (`/hooks/{token}`) and, when given a secret, signs the exact bytes it sends in the `X-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header. The API key is never sent to hooks.

```java
// In your HTTP handler: rawBody is the body exactly as received, headers any Map of header names to values.
String outcome;
try {
    WebhookEvent event = client.verifyWebhook(rawBody, headers); // uses TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET
    if (event instanceof WebhookEventAutomationRunCompleted) {
        System.out.println("run finished: " + ((WebhookEventAutomationRunCompleted) event).data());
    }
    outcome = event.type();
} catch (WebhookVerificationException e) {
    outcome = "rejected"; // answer 400: e.reason() tells why
}

// Post an event to an incoming hook; the body is signed in the X-Signature header.
AutomationHookAccepted accepted = client.sendHook("hook-token",
    HookRequest.json(Map.of("order", "1532", "amount_tiyn", 4500000))
        .secret("hook-secret")
        .eventId("order-1532")
        .build());
```

`verifyWebhook` uses the client's webhook secret; `TungoWebhooks.verify(body, headers, secret)` and `WebhookVerifier` work without a client. Pass the raw body exactly as received: every `verify` method takes it as a `String` or, better, as the `byte[]` your framework read from the socket. `TungoWebhooks.verifyHookSignature` checks the `X-Signature` of an incoming hook.

## Money

The API expresses amounts in tiyn (1/100 of a tenge) as 64-bit integers. The money helper converts decimal strings and exact decimal values to tiyn without floating-point error, rounding half away from zero (`"1.005"` → `101`), and formats tiyn for display (`4500000` → `45 000,00 ₸`). Invalid input raises a typed error.

```java
long tiyn = TungoMoney.toTiyn("1234.565");                 // 123457
long same = TungoMoney.toTiyn(new BigDecimal("1234.565")); // 123457
String text = TungoMoney.formatTiyn(tiyn);                 // "1 234,57 ₸"
boolean valid = TungoMoney.isValidBinIin("990140000017");  // true
```

Amounts are whole tiyn in a `long`. `toTiyn` takes a decimal `String` or a `BigDecimal` and rounds half away from zero; bad input raises `ValidationException`.

## Async client

`client.async()` is a view of the same client whose methods return `CompletableFuture`. It is not non-blocking I/O: each async method runs the blocking call on an executor, so a call occupies one thread until its response is read (a streaming method until the stream is open, a waiting helper until the wait ends). By default the executor is a pool of daemon threads owned by the client and limited to 64 threads (`asyncMaxThreads(n)`); further calls wait in a queue. Pass your own with `asyncExecutor(...)`, for example `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()` on Java 21 or later. Cancelling a future interrupts the call; on Java 16 and later that also closes the connection at once, on Java 11 to 15 the abandoned connection is closed when the request timeout passes.

```java
CompletableFuture<String> name = client.async().companies().get("co_...")
    .thenApply(Company::name);
```

## Models

Every request and response is an immutable class with a builder. A required property has a plain getter; an optional or nullable one returns `Optional<T>`; a request property that may be sent as an explicit `null` is a `JsonNullable<T>` (absent, null or a value). Enums are open: an unknown value is kept (`value()`, `isKnown()`). A `oneOf` with a discriminator is an interface with one class per variant, an `Unknown` variant and a `Visitor`; other unions are wrappers with `isX()` / `asX()` accessors. Properties this version of the SDK does not know are kept in `additionalProperties()`.

Decoding is tolerant of additions and strict about types. Unknown properties, enum values and union variants never fail. A value of the wrong JSON type does: a fraction or a string where an integer is expected, a number where a string is expected. A required list or map is never `null`: a response without it is a `DecodeException`. Other required properties are not checked when decoding, so the getter of a required scalar or object returns `null` if the API left it out.

```java
ChatMessageRequest request = ChatMessageRequest.builder()
    .message("Продолжим")
    .dialogId(JsonNullable.ofNull()) // sends "dialog_id": null; leave it out to omit the property
    .build();

String description = event.accept(new ChatEvent.Visitor<String>() {
    @Override
    public String visitText(ChatEventText value) {
        return "text " + value.delta();
    }

    @Override
    public String visitDefault(ChatEvent value) {
        return "event " + value.type(); // every other variant, known or not
    }
});
```

## Raw responses

Every plain method has a `...WithResponse` variant that returns `ApiResponse<T>`: status, headers, request id and the rate limit of that very response. A `Page` and a stream expose the same through `response()`.

```java
ApiResponse<Company> response = client.companies().getWithResponse("co_...", RequestOptions.none());
String requestId = response.requestId().orElse("?");
long remaining = response.rateLimit().map(limit -> limit.remaining()).orElse(-1L);
Company company = response.body();
```

## Waiting for long-running work

`waitForRun`, `runScenarioAndWait` and `waitForBatch` poll (1 s growing to 5 s) until the work reaches a final state or the deadline passes (`WaitTimeoutException`).

```java
AutomationRunDetail run = client.runScenarioAndWait("co_...", "scenario-id", null, options);
System.out.println(run.state().value()); // done, error, skipped or cancelled
```

## API reference

Generated from the Tungo Platform API contract: **13 resources, 85 methods, 22 webhook event types**.

| Resource | Description | Methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.workspaces()` | Organisations (workspaces) the API key can access | `list` |
| `client.companies()` | Companies of an organisation and their profiles | `list` · `get` |
| `client.platform()` | Platform balance, ledger, usage reports, limits, audit log and model rates | `listUsageRates` · `getAccount` · `getAudit / getAuditAll` · `getLedger / getLedgerAll` · `listLimits` · `listRequests / listRequestsAll` · `getUsage` |
| `client.apiKeys()` | The current API key and its usage statistics | `getCurrent` · `getCurrentUsage` · `getUsage` |
| `client.webhooks()` | Outgoing webhooks of an organisation (Svix): endpoints, event catalogue, deliveries and signature check | `listEndpoints / listEndpointsAll` · `createEndpoint` · `getEndpoint` · `updateEndpoint` · `deleteEndpoint` · `listEndpointAttempts / listEndpointAttemptsAll` · `rotateEndpointSecret` · `testEndpoint` · `listEventTypes` · `listMessages / listMessagesAll` · `listMessageAttempts / listMessageAttemptsAll` · `resendMessage` · `getUsage` |
| `client.chat()` | Conversations with the AI accountant: questions, streaming chat (SSE), token counting and history | `list / listAll` · `create / createStream` · `countTokens` · `listMentions` · `listSuggestions` · `get` · `update` · `delete` · `answer / answerStream` · `listEvents` · `stop` |
| `client.proposals()` | Documents proposed by the AI accountant: review, approval for posting to 1C, and rejection | `list / listAll` · `approveBatch` · `get` · `approve` · `reject` · `requestApproval` |
| `client.feed()` | The company's feed of events and proposals (pages and a live SSE stream) | `get / getAll` · `listEvents` |
| `client.batches()` | Processing batches for bank statements, incoming e-invoices and DirectBank | `list / listAll` · `createBankStatement` · `createEsfPurchases` · `get` · `listEvents` · `stop` · `getSummary` · `listStatements / listStatementsAll` · `pollDirectbank` |
| `client.esf()` | Incoming and outgoing electronic invoices (the ESF system) | `getIncoming / getIncomingAll` · `getOutgoing / getOutgoingAll` |
| `client.forms()` | Tax forms (FNO 100.00 and others): building, ISNA checks and data gaps | `list` · `build` · `listDataGaps` · `getIsna` · `listNotes` |
| `client.onec()` | Status of the company's connection to its 1C database | `getStatus` |
| `client.automations()` | Company automations: incoming hooks, scenarios, step chains, runs and the AI autonomy level | `postHook` · `listHooks` · `createHook` · `getHook` · `updateHook` · `deleteHook` · `rotateHook` · `testHook` · `listRuns / listRunsAll` · `getRun` · `cancelRun` · `retryRun` · `listScenarios` · `createScenario` · `getScenario` · `putScenario` · `updateScenario` · `deleteScenario` · `runScenario` · `getState` · `putState` · `getAutonomy` · `putAutonomy` |

## Versioning and support

This library follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). While the major version is 0, a minor release may contain breaking changes; they are always listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-java/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). This README describes version 0.3.0.

The code is generated: please report problems and ideas in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-java/issues) rather than opening pull requests against generated files. To report a vulnerability, follow the [security policy](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-java/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
